views.name: users_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "first_name" AS first_name,
       "last_name" AS last_name,
       "email" AS email,
       "age" AS age,
       "gender" AS gender,
       "state" AS state,
       "street_address" AS street_address,
       "postal_code" AS postal_code,
       "city" AS city,
       "country" AS country,
       "latitude" AS latitude,
       "longitude" AS longitude,
       "traffic_source" AS traffic_source,
       "created_at" AS created_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS

params.description: One-row-per-user normalized view exposing user profile and signup attributes for filtering, joining, and composing user-level analyses.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve user profile information (name, contact, location) for display or export. | Filter or segment users by demographic or source (age, gender, traffic_source, country, state, city). | Join to order, event, or session-level data to produce user-level aggregates (e.g., orders per user, revenue per user) — when joining, ensure cardinality safety as described. | Seed user-level aggregations (e.g., lifetime value, first purchase date) or enrich other datasets with user attributes. | Build funnels or cohort analyses by joining created_at with event/order timestamps (user signup time).
params.output_schema: id: Unique identifier for the user. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.id | first_name: User's first name. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.first_name | last_name: User's last name. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.last_name | email: User's email address. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.email | age: User's age (as recorded). Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.age | gender: User's gender (as recorded). Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.gender | state: State/region of the user's address. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.state | street_address: Street address of the user. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.street_address | postal_code: Postal / ZIP code. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.postal_code | city: City of the user's address. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.city | country: Country of the user. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.country | latitude: Latitude coordinate for user's address (if present). Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.latitude | longitude: Longitude coordinate for user's address (if present). Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.longitude | traffic_source: Acquisition/traffic source for the user (e.g., ad, organic). Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.traffic_source | created_at: Timestamp when the user record / signup was created. Derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS.created_at
params.metric: No derived numeric metrics are computed in this view. All columns are pass-through attributes from the USERS table. | If used as a base for aggregations, typical derived metrics to define elsewhere include: | orders_count = COUNT(DISTINCT orders_base.id) when joining orders_base on users_base.id | revenue = SUM(order_items_base.price * order_items_base.quantity) when joining order_items_base (aggregated to order or user level first) | first_event_at = MIN(events_base.occurred_at) when aggregating events_base per user
params.composition: Safe joins (cardinality-safe — will not duplicate users_base rows/measures): |  - Join to orders_base ON orders_base.user_id = users_base.id AFTER aggregating orders_base to one row per user (e.g., orders_per_user_agg) or when selecting order-level detail intentionally (understanding it creates one-to-many rows). Use orders_per_user_agg because it is one-row-per-user, so joining preserves users_base cardinality. |  - Join to user_event_sessions_agg ON user_event_sessions_agg.user_id = users_base.id because user_event_sessions_agg is aggregated to one row per user (or per user-session depending on that view's grain) — ensure its grain matches the desired result (one-row-per-user is safe). |  - Join to product_sales_agg or orders_per_user_agg when they are aggregated to user-level keys; these are safe because they are pre-aggregated and will not multiply rows. | Unsafe joins (will duplicate users_base rows/measures unless you re-aggregate first): |  - Do NOT directly join users_base to orders_base (orders table) on users_base.id if orders_base is one-to-many (multiple orders per user) unless you intend to produce order-level rows. Doing so will multiply user rows and any user-level measures. |  - Do NOT directly join users_base to order_items_base or products_base or events_base without first aggregating those tables to the user-level, because they are naturally one-to-many (order_items per order, events per user/session, products per order_item). |  - Do NOT join users_base to order_items_enriched or user_lifecycle_summary (JOIN views) without understanding their grains — if those views are one-to-many to users, aggregate them first. | Guidance for correct composition: |  - When you need user-level metrics (counts, sums, first/last timestamps), aggregate the child table by user_id (e.g., using orders_per_user_agg or SUM/COUNT with GROUP BY user_id) and then LEFT JOIN to users_base ON users_base.id = agg.user_id. This preserves one-row-per-user and avoids double-counting. |  - If you need event/order-level detail for a subset of users, filter users_base first, then join to the one-to-many table and perform aggregations afterwards, being explicit about GROUP BY users_base.id when producing user-level outputs. |  - Use LEFT JOIN when enriching users_base with optional aggregated data to retain users with no matching child records.

views.description: Cleaned projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS exposing canonical user identifiers, profile attributes and created timestamp. Use this as the normalized users dimension for joins and user-level aggregates. | Use for: user demographics by geography/traffic_source; new users per period; churn or cohort analysis joined to events/orders

views.name: orders_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT "order_id" AS order_id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "status" AS status,
       "gender" AS gender,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "returned_at" AS returned_at,
       "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       "num_of_item" AS num_of_item
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS

params.description: One-row-per-order canonical view of orders with user, status, timestamps, and item count — used as the normalized base for order-level analysis.
params.when_to_use: Return order-level facts (counts, lists) such as number of orders, distribution of order statuses, or timeline analysis by order created_at. | Compose order-level KPIs with other dimensions (user, fulfillment center) when preserving one-row-per-order granularity. | Build aggregates keyed by order_id or user_id (after grouping) such as orders per user, average items per order, or order-level lifecycle metrics (time to ship/deliver/return). | Serve as the base for enrichment joins (order_items_enriched) or for joining pre-aggregated order-level results into higher level summaries.
params.output_schema: order_id: surrogate/primary key for each order — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.order_id | user_id: identifier of the user who placed the order — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.user_id | status: current order status (e.g., pending, shipped, delivered, returned) — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.status | gender: customer gender snapshot on the order row (copied into orders table) — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.gender | created_at: timestamp when the order was created — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.created_at | returned_at: timestamp when the order was returned (nullable) — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.returned_at | shipped_at: timestamp when the order was shipped (nullable) — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.shipped_at | delivered_at: timestamp when the order was delivered (nullable) — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.delivered_at | num_of_item: integer count of items on the order as stored in orders table (order-level item count) — derives from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS.num_of_item
params.metric: order_count = COUNT(order_id)  -- aggregate count of orders when grouped at any higher grain | sum_num_of_item = SUM(num_of_item)  -- total items summed across orders; safe only when aggregation groups do not duplicate order_id | avg_items_per_order = AVG(num_of_item)  -- average number of items per order computed from num_of_item at order grain | time_to_ship = MIN(DATEDIFF(second, created_at, shipped_at)) over grouped orders  -- can be computed per-order as shipped_at - created_at when both timestamps present | time_to_deliver = MIN(DATEDIFF(second, shipped_at, delivered_at)) over grouped orders  -- per-order delivered_at - shipped_at when present | returned_flag = CASE WHEN returned_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END  -- can be aggregated as SUM(returned_flag) to get returned orders count
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on orders_base.user_id = users_base.user_id — safe because users_base is one-row-per-user; joining preserves one-row-per-order (orders are not duplicated). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_per_user_agg on orders_base.user_id = orders_per_user_agg.user_id — safe for enriching order rows with pre-aggregated user-level metrics because the aggregate is one-row-per-user. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to distribution_centers_base on appropriate key (if present) when distribution_centers_base is one-row-per-distribution_center — safe to add center attributes (does not duplicate orders). | do NOT join directly to order_items_base or order_items_enriched without re-aggregating order_items to order-level first (e.g., SUM(quantity) GROUP BY order_id) — those are one-to-many to orders and will multiply order-level measures like num_of_item and order_count if joined at row-level. | do NOT join to products_base or inventory_items_base directly unless you ensure a single representative product/inventory row per order (e.g., pre-aggregate or filter to a single item) — products and inventory are many-to-many/one-to-many relative to orders through order_items and would duplicate order rows. | when needing order-level summaries that include item-level measures, first aggregate order_items_base or order_items_enriched to order_id (SUM, COUNT, MAX as appropriate) and then join the aggregated result to orders_base on order_id — this preserves correct aggregates and avoids double counting. | joining to events_base or latest_event_per_session is safe only when those event views are pre-aggregated to one-row-per-order (or joined on a different key that is one-to-one). Raw events are many-to-one and will duplicate orders if joined directly. | If composing further aggregates (e.g., orders per user), always group by the target key (user_id) and aggregate orders_base measures (COUNT(order_id), SUM(num_of_item)) instead of relying on joins that may increase cardinality.

views.description: Normalized projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS exposing order-level identifiers, timestamps, status and basic measures. Use for order-level analytics and safe joins to ORDER_ITEMS or USERS. | Use for: orders over time; fulfillment latency (created -> shipped/delivered); returns rate at order level; join to ORDER_ITEMS for item-level metrics

views.name: order_items_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "order_id" AS order_id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "product_id" AS product_id,
       "inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
       "status" AS status,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       "returned_at" AS returned_at,
       "sale_price" AS sale_price
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
grain: id -- one row per order item (order line)

params.description: Provides one row per order item (order line) with its identifiers, lifecycle timestamps, status, and sale price — answers questions about individual order items and forms a safe base for aggregations and joins to one-sided dimensions.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve details for specific order items (by id, order_id, product_id, user_id, inventory_item_id). | Compute aggregations at the order-item grain (counts, sums of sale_price, averages) or compose higher-level aggregates (per-order, per-user, per-product) by aggregating this view. | Filter order items by lifecycle status or time windows (created_at, shipped_at, delivered_at, returned_at). | Join to dimension-like tables (users, products, inventory_items, orders) on their keys to enrich order-item rows without duplicating measures, as long as the join is one-to-one from the other side.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the order item (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.id) | order_id: foreign key referencing the containing order (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.order_id) | user_id: foreign key referencing the buyer/owner of the order item (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.user_id) | product_id: foreign key referencing the product sold on this order item (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.product_id) | inventory_item_id: foreign key referencing the inventory item (stock unit) for this order item (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.inventory_item_id) | status: lifecycle status of the order item (e.g., created, shipped, delivered, returned) (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.status) | created_at: timestamp when the order item was created (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.created_at) | shipped_at: timestamp when the order item was shipped (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.shipped_at) | delivered_at: timestamp when the order item was delivered (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.delivered_at) | returned_at: timestamp when the order item was returned (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.returned_at) | sale_price: sale price paid for this order item (monetary measure) (derived from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS.sale_price)
params.metric: count_order_items = COUNT(id) -- use when aggregating rows from this view; count of order item rows | sum_sale_price = SUM(sale_price) -- total revenue at order-item grain (monetary sum) | avg_sale_price = AVG(sale_price) -- average sale price per order item | min_created_at = MIN(created_at) -- earliest creation timestamp in an aggregation | max_created_at = MAX(created_at) -- latest creation timestamp in an aggregation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on order_items_base.user_id = users_base.id — safe because users_base is one row per user (one-to-many from users to order_items) so joining users enriches each order_item without duplicating order-item measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on order_items_base.order_id = orders_base.id — safe because orders_base is one row per order (one-to-many from orders to order_items); order_item measures remain at order-item grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base on order_items_base.product_id = products_base.id — safe because products_base is one row per product (one-to-many from products to order_items). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to inventory_items_base on order_items_base.inventory_item_id = inventory_items_base.id — safe because inventory_items_base is one row per inventory_item (one-to-many to order_items) and does not duplicate order-item rows. | do NOT join directly (without re-aggregation or de-duplication) to any table or view that is one-to-many from order_items_base (i.e., where a single order_item.id would match multiple rows) because that would multiply this view's rows and thus incorrectly inflate measures like count_order_items or sum_sale_price. Examples to avoid: events_base (if events are tracked per order_item and multiple events exist per item) or any activity/log table with multiple rows per order_item. | when composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., per-order, per-user, per-product), aggregate order_items_base first (GROUP BY order_id/user_id/product_id) producing measures (COUNT(id), SUM(sale_price), etc.), then join that aggregated result to other tables to prevent duplication. | if you must join to a one-to-many child (e.g., events_base which may have multiple events per order_item), either (a) aggregate the child to one row per order_item (e.g., COUNT, MAX timestamps) before joining, or (b) join then re-aggregate back to the desired grain, ensuring you use appropriate DISTINCT or SUM of aggregates to avoid double counting sale_price.

views.description: Normalized projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS exposing line-item identifiers, foreign keys, lifecycle timestamps, status and sale_price for item-level analysis. | Use for: item-level revenue, returns, and fulfillment; join to PRODUCTS or INVENTORY_ITEMS to enrich product attributes; per-item lifetime (created -> shipped/delivered/returned)

views.name: products_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "cost" AS cost,
       "category" AS category,
       "name" AS name,
       "brand" AS brand,
       "retail_price" AS retail_price,
       "department" AS department,
       "sku" AS sku,
       "distribution_center_id" AS distribution_center_id
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS

params.description: One row per product with product attributes and pricing/cost information — answers product-level attribute, pricing, and inventory-location membership questions.
params.when_to_use: Look up product attributes (name, brand, category, department, sku) for display or enrichment. | Calculate product-level gross margin or price-based metrics when combined with sales (e.g., join product to order_items and aggregate sales by product). | Filter or slice downstream aggregates by distribution_center_id (i.e., which distribution center a product is stocked/assigned to). | Serve as the canonical product dimension when joining to fact tables (orders, order_items, inventory_items, events) — provided joins preserve product grain or re-aggregate when adding one-to-many children.
params.output_schema: id: Unique product identifier — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.id | cost: Product unit cost (input cost) — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.cost | category: Product category classification — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.category | name: Product name/title — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.name | brand: Product brand — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.brand | retail_price: Product retail price (list price) — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.retail_price | department: Higher-level department for the product — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.department | sku: Stock-keeping unit — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.sku | distribution_center_id: Identifier of the distribution center associated with the product — sourced from THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS.distribution_center_id
params.metric: Note: products_base is a normalized (NORM) dimensional view at product grain and does not define aggregated metrics itself. It supplies base columns usable in metrics. Examples of derived metrics to compute after joining/aggregating: | product_retail_price = retail_price  -- pass-through value per product | product_cost = cost  -- pass-through value per product | product_gross_margin_value = SUM((order_items.quantity * (products_base.retail_price - products_base.cost))) when joined to order_items and aggregated at desired grain | product_gross_margin_pct = (SUM(order_items.quantity * (products_base.retail_price - products_base.cost)) / NULLIF(SUM(order_items.quantity * products_base.retail_price),0)) when joined to order_items and aggregated
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to distribution_centers_base on distribution_center_id = distribution_centers_base.id — safe because products_base has one row per product; joining to a distribution center (dimension) will not duplicate product rows as long as distribution_centers_base has one row per distribution_center_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_per_user_agg or product_sales_agg only when those are pre-aggregated to product_id (or higher) to avoid duplication — safe if the aggregate's grain is product_id or higher-level (e.g., product+date). | do NOT directly join products_base to one-to-many tables/views such as order_items_base, orders_base, inventory_items_base, events_base, or order_items_enriched without aggregation on the one-to-many side first — those joins will multiply product rows because order_items (and events/inventory items) can have many rows per product. Instead, aggregate the fact (e.g., SUM(quantity), SUM(revenue) grouped by product_id) in the fact table/view, then join the aggregated result to products_base. | When composing with sibling JOIN views (e.g., order_items_enriched or user_lifecycle_summary) confirm their output grain. If the sibling view is at a finer grain than product (many rows per product), either (a) aggregate the sibling view to product_id before joining, or (b) join using DISTINCT product ids and then re-attach metrics from an aggregation step. | When joining to RANK/WIN views (latest_event_per_session, top_products_by_revenue_rank, orders_fulfillment_latency) check their grain and ensure they are reduced to product-level or a 1:1 key with products_base before joining; otherwise re-aggregate or filter to a single representative row per product. | Safe pattern example: SELECT p.*, s.total_quantity, s.total_revenue FROM products_base p LEFT JOIN (SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(quantity*price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items_base GROUP BY product_id) s ON p.id = s.product_id — this preserves product grain and avoids measure duplication.

views.description: Projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS exposing product dimension attributes and pricing. Use for product-level joins and catalogue analytics. | Use for: product catalog reports; margin calculations when joined to order items (sale_price - cost); distribution center distribution of SKUs

views.name: inventory_items_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "product_id" AS product_id,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "sold_at" AS sold_at,
       "cost" AS cost,
       "product_category" AS product_category,
       "product_name" AS product_name,
       "product_brand" AS product_brand,
       "product_retail_price" AS product_retail_price,
       "product_department" AS product_department,
       "product_sku" AS product_sku,
       "product_distribution_center_id" AS product_distribution_center_id
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS
grain: id -- one row per physical inventory item

params.description: One row per physical inventory item, describing its product, cost, timestamps, and distribution center — answers questions about inventory-level attributes and supports counting/aggregating inventory by product, status, time, and location.
params.when_to_use: Count or aggregate inventory items (e.g., total on-hand, total cost) by product attributes, distribution center, or time (created_at/sold_at). | Filter or slice inventory at the item-level before joining to orders, sales, or product dimensions. | As a base (normalized) source when building enriched item-level joins or item-level aggregates (e.g., inventory turnover, SKU-level stock counts).
params.output_schema: id: Unique identifier for the physical inventory item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.id. | product_id: FK linking this item to a product. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_id. | created_at: Timestamp when the inventory item was created/added. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.created_at. | sold_at: Timestamp when the item was sold (nullable if not sold). Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.sold_at. | cost: Monetary cost for this inventory item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.cost. | product_category: Product category text/label for the product linked to this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_category. | product_name: Product name for the product linked to this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_name. | product_brand: Brand for the product linked to this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_brand. | product_retail_price: Retail price for the product linked to this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_retail_price. | product_department: Department for the product linked to this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_department. | product_sku: SKU code for the product linked to this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_sku. | product_distribution_center_id: FK to the distribution center that holds/handled this item. Derived from INVENTORY_ITEMS.product_distribution_center_id.
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(id) -- count of inventory items (grain = one row per physical inventory item) | total_cost = SUM(cost) -- sum of cost across selected items | avg_cost = AVG(cost) -- average cost per selected item | sold_count = COUNT(CASE WHEN sold_at IS NOT NULL THEN id END) -- number of items sold | unsold_count = COUNT(CASE WHEN sold_at IS NULL THEN id END) -- number of items not sold
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base on product_id = products_base.id — safe because inventory_items_base is one row per physical item; joining to the products_base (one row per product) will not duplicate inventory item rows (product is a dimension). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to distribution_centers_base on product_distribution_center_id = distribution_centers_base.id — safe because distribution_centers_base is one row per distribution center (dimension), so this will not multiply inventory item rows. | do NOT naively join to order_items_base or orders_base without re-aggregation or explicit matching keys that ensure 1:1 — those are one-to-many relative to inventory items in common schemas (an item may be referenced by zero or one order_item depending on implementation, but order_items_base is typically many order lines per product or SKU). To avoid duplicating inventory measures, either: |   - aggregate order/order_item measures to the inventory item level first (e.g., count of order_items linked to inventory item id) and then join, or |   - join on a guaranteed 1:1 key (if such key exists in your schema) or use EXISTS/subqueries to filter inventory items by order membership instead of joining that multiplies rows. | do NOT join to sibling aggregated views (orders_per_user_agg, product_sales_agg, user_event_sessions_agg, etc.) expecting to preserve item-level measures unless you re-aggregate inventory_items_base to the same grain as the target aggregate first — joining item-level rows to an aggregate that is at a coarser grain will multiply rows unless the aggregate is joined by its grouping keys and you aggregate inventory measures to those keys beforehand. | When composing metrics: to compute metrics at product/SKU/DC/date grains, first GROUP BY the desired keys from inventory_items_base (e.g., product_id, product_sku, product_distribution_center_id, DATE(created_at)) and compute SUM(cost), COUNT(id), AVG(cost), etc., then join that aggregated result to other dimensions/aggregates. This guarantees cardinality safety because the aggregation collapses the one-row-per-item grain into the target grain before combining with other sources.

views.description: Projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS exposing one row per physical inventory item with lifecycle timestamps and denormalized product attributes. Use for inventory turnover and sold-item-level analytics. | Use for: inventory turnover and time-to-sell; cost-of-goods-sold when linked to sold items; compare denormalized product attributes to PRODUCTS dimension

views.name: events_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "sequence_number" AS sequence_number,
       "session_id" AS session_id,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "ip_address" AS ip_address,
       "city" AS city,
       "state" AS state,
       "postal_code" AS postal_code,
       "browser" AS browser,
       "traffic_source" AS traffic_source,
       "uri" AS uri,

If you need order-level enrichment for events (e.g., attribute an event to an order), pre-aggregate or filter orders to a one-row-per-order-key result and join on that key. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_per_user_agg on events_base.user_id = orders_per_user_agg.user_id — safe because orders_per_user_agg is an aggregate that is one-row-per-user; it will not duplicate event rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base, order_items_base, inventory_items_base, distribution_centers_base only when you have a clear one-to-one key per event (for example if an event contains product_id and that maps one-to-one to products_base.id). params.description: Lists distribution centers with their identifiers and geographic coordinates; answers questions about where distribution centers are and provides a one-row-per-center base to join or aggregate against.

views.name: order_items_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT oi.id AS id,
       oi.order_id AS order_id,
       oi.user_id AS user_id,
       oi.product_id AS product_id,
       oi.inventory_item_id AS inventory_item_id,

FROM order_items_base oi
LEFT JOIN orders_base o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN products_base p
  ON oi.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN inventory_items_base ii
  ON oi.inventory_item_id = ii.id

params.description: Enriched, line-level order items combining order, product and inventory attributes — answers questions about individual order item lines and supports safe aggregation/composition at the order-item grain.
params.when_to_use: Report or analyze metrics at the order-item (line) level, e.g., revenue, cost, margins, fulfillment timestamps, and lifecycle of a specific order item. | Slice/order-line level breakdowns by product attributes (name, brand, category), inventory attributes (sku, distribution center), or order attributes (order status, order creation time). | Build higher-level aggregates (per order, per user, per product, per distribution center) by aggregating this view — use this as the canonical line-level source.

derived from orders_base.created_at | product_name: product name — derived from products_base.name (via oi.product_id = p.id) | product_brand: product brand — derived from products_base.brand | (unit cost) — derived from products_base.cost | inventory_sku: SKU of the inventory item that fulfilled the line — derived from inventory_items_base.product_sku (via oi.inventory_item_id = ii.id) | params.grounded_columns: order_items_base.id | order_items_base.order_id | order_items_base.user_id | order_items_base.product_id | order_items_base.inventory_item_id | order_items_base.status | order_items_base.created_at | order_items_base.shipped_at | order_items_base.delivered_at | order_items_base.returned_at | order_items_base.sale_price | orders_base.order_id | orders_base.status | orders_base.created_at | products_base.id | products_base.name | products_base.brand | products_base.category | products_base.retail_price | products_base.cost | inventory_items_base.id | inventory_items_base.product_sku | inventory_items_base.product_distribution_center_id

If sale_price is per-line and cost is per-unit, caller must ensure consistent semantics before aggregating margin. | line_margin = (sale_price - product_cost)  -- simple per-line margin expression; aggregate after verifying unit consistency | fulfilled = (shipped_at IS NOT NULL)  -- boolean indicator whether this line has shipped; evaluate per-row | delivered = (delivered_at IS NOT NULL)  -- boolean indicator whether this line has been delivered
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on order_id — safe because this view already LEFT JOINs orders_base by oi.order_id = o.order_id; orders_base is 1 row per order (orders_base.order_id), so joining to orders or other 1:1 order-level dimensions will NOT duplicate order-item rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base on product_id — safe because this view already LEFT JOINs products_base by oi.product_id = p.id; products_base is 1 row per product, so joining to product-level dimensions will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to inventory_items_base on inventory_item_id — safe because this view already LEFT JOINs inventory_items_base by oi.inventory_item_id = ii.id; inventory_items_base is 1 row per inventory item, so joining to inventory-level dimensions will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to distribution_centers_base on inventory_distribution_center_id = distribution_centers_base.id — safe if distribution_centers_base is 1 row per distribution center. views.name: orders_per_user_agg

       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
       SUM(o.num_of_item) AS items_ordered,
       MIN(o.created_at) AS first_order_at,
       MAX(o.created_at) AS last_order_at
FROM orders_base o
GROUP BY o.user_id

params.description: One row per user summarizing that user's orders: total distinct orders, total items ordered, and timestamps of first and last order.
params.when_to_use: Find per-user order activity summaries (counts, totals, first/last order times). | Join user demographic data to order summary (one-to-one by user) for reporting or ML features. | Compose into higher-level aggregates (e.g., cohort metrics, percentiles) where a single per-user order row is the correct grain. | Use as a feature table in models that require per-user order history summaries.
params.output_schema: user_id: the user identifier this row summarizes. Derived from orders_base.user_id (SELECT o.user_id AS user_id). | orders_count: number of distinct orders for this user. Derived from COUNT(DISTINCT orders_base.order_id). | items_ordered: total number of ordered items for this user. Derived from SUM(orders_base.num_of_item). | first_order_at: timestamp of the earliest order for this user. Derived from MIN(orders_base.created_at). | last_order_at: timestamp of the latest order for this user. Derived from MAX(orders_base.created_at).

If the other view is already one-row-per-user, joining on user_id is safe. | do NOT join orders_per_user_agg directly to orders_base (or order_items_base, order_items_enriched, order_items_base, events_base, inventory_items_base, product tables) without re-aggregation on those tables first — those are one-to-many from user_id and will multiply orders_per_user_agg measures and produce incorrect sums/counts. | do NOT join to order_items_base or order_items_enriched on user_id without re-aggregating order_items to user-level first — joining raw order-item rows to this per-user summary will duplicate the per-user aggregates (orders_count, items_ordered) proportional to the number of item rows. | If you must combine with a one-to-many table (events_base, order_items_base, order_items_enriched, products_base, inventory_items_base), either: (a) aggregate that table to user_id (or to the same grain) before joining, or (b) join at a lower grain and then re-aggregate the combined result to the desired grain. This ensures measures from orders_per_user_agg are not incorrectly multiplied. | When composing with ranking/window outputs (latest_event_per_session, top_products_by_revenue_rank, orders_fulfillment_latency), ensure those outputs are first reduced to user_id (one row per user) before joining, or join on keys that guarantee one-to-one relationship. | Planner note: the base measures in this view (orders_count, items_ordered) are already user-level aggregates computed solely from orders_base grouped by user_id. Any join that preserves one-row-per-user (one-to-one or left join to one-row-per-user) will not require re-weighting. Any join to multi-row-per-user sources requires re-aggregation to avoid duplicating these measures.

views.description: Aggregated order-level measures per user: order count, total items ordered (sum num_of_item), first and last order timestamps. Use to profile customer activity and to join back to user cohorts. | Use for: customer RFM-style features; active users vs dormant users; join to users_base for demographics

views.name: product_sales_agg

       COUNT(1) AS items_sold,
       SUM(COALESCE(oi.sale_price,0)) AS total_sales,
       AVG(oi.sale_price) AS avg_sale_price
FROM order_items_base oi
GROUP BY oi.product_id
grain: product_id -- one row per product summarizing sales

params.description: Per-product aggregated sales metrics (one row per product summarizing count, sum, and average of sale_price from order_items_base).
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard showing sales performance per product (items sold, total revenue, average sale price). | As a pre-aggregated building block when computing product-level KPIs (e.g., revenue share, rank by revenue) without re-scanning order_items_base. | Joining product-level metrics to product dimension (products_base) or displaying product attributes alongside sales metrics. | Composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., category-level revenue) by re-aggregating these per-product rows.

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base on product_id — safe because product_sales_agg is one-row-per-product (product_id) so joining to the product dimension (one row per product_id) will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to top_products_by_revenue_rank (RANK) on product_id — safe when that rank view is also one-row-per-product, because it will not duplicate the product_sales_agg measures. | do NOT join directly to order_items_base (or order_items_enriched) without re-aggregation — those are potentially many rows per product and will multiply items_sold/total_sales unless you re-aggregate (e.g., SUM over matching product_ids) or join on a 1:1 key. | do NOT join to views/tables that are one-to-many with respect to product_id (for example, an events table that logs many events per product) without re-aggregating the many-side first, because that will duplicate this view's aggregated measures. | safe composition pattern for computing category-level totals: join product_sales_agg to products_base on product_id to get product -> category mapping (1:1), then GROUP BY category and SUM(total_sales) and SUM(items_sold) — re-aggregation prevents duplication. | when combining with other product-level aggregates (e.g., inventory_items_base summarized per product), ensure the other side is also one-row-per-product or aggregated to product_id before joining; joining two different one-row-per-product views on product_id is safe. | if joining to orders_per_user_agg, users_base, orders_base, or user_event_sessions_agg, ensure keys used do not create many-to-one multiplicative relationships — prefer joining via products_base (product attributes) or pre-aggregating the many side to product_id before join.

params.metric: events_in_session = COUNT(1) over rows in events_base grouped by (events_base.user_id, events_base.session_id) | session_start_at = MIN(events_base.created_at) grouped by (events_base.user_id, events_base.session_id) | session_end_at = MAX(events_base.created_at) grouped by (events_base.user_id, events_base.session_id) | distinct_uris = COUNT(DISTINCT events_base.uri) grouped by (events_base.user_id, events_base.session_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on user_id — safe because users_base is normalized (one row per user) so joining on user_id will not duplicate session-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_event_per_session or other session-level views keyed by (user_id, session_id) — safe because they share the same session grain (one row per session) so measures remain unduplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_per_user_agg only after aligning grain (this view is per-session; orders_per_user_agg is per-user). If you need session attribution of orders, first aggregate or filter orders to session-level (or join orders to a session mapping) before joining; direct join on user_id will duplicate session rows across orders or, conversely, duplicate order metrics across sessions. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as order_items_base, products_base, or order_items_enriched on user_id or session_id without re-aggregation — those are many rows per session or per order and will multiply events_in_session and distinct_uris unless you first aggregate the one-to-many side to the session (user_id, session_id) grain or to user_id only depending on desired result. | do NOT join to events_base (the base table) back onto this aggregate on user_id/session_id — that would reintroduce the original many rows and duplicate aggregated measures unless you only join via EXISTS or other non-multiplicative patterns. | safe composition pattern examples: | - To get per-user totals: aggregate this view by user_id (SUM(events_in_session), MIN(session_start_at), MAX(session_end_at), SUM(distinct_uris) or COUNT(DISTINCT session_id || uri) depending on precise distinct semantics). | - To attach user attributes: JOIN users_base ub ON user_id = ub.user_id (one-to-one) — session measures remain correct. | - To enrich sessions with a single best event per session: JOIN latest_event_per_session lv ON (user_id, session_id) = (lv.user_id, lv.session_id) — safe because latest_event_per_session is ranked to one row per session. | - To combine with orders: if you need orders per session, first compute orders_per_session (group orders/order_items by user_id, session_id) or filter orders that have a single order->session mapping; then JOIN orders_per_session ON (user_id, session_id). Do NOT join orders_base or order_items_base directly without session-level aggregation.

views.description: Aggregated session-level metrics per user-session pairing: event count, first/last event timestamp, and distinct URIs visited. Useful for funnel and session analytics. | Use for: session duration and engagement; pre-purchase session characteristics when joined to orders

views.name: latest_event_per_session
views.body_sql:
SELECT id,
       user_id,
       session_id,
       sequence_number,
       created_at,
       ip_address,
       city,
       state,
       postal_code,
       browser,
       traffic_source,
       uri,
       event_type,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, sequence_number DESC) AS rn
FROM events_base
grain: session_id, rn -- multiple rows per session but rn=1 indicates latest event

semantic_filters.rn: use rn = 1 to select the latest event per session downstream

params.description: Provides the latest event row for each session (rn = 1 is the most-recent event of that session), enabling queries about a session's final event or building aggregations anchored at the last event per session.
params.when_to_use: Find the most recent event details for each session (e.g., last page visited, last event_type, last IP or geo for session). | Build session-level metrics anchored on the final event (e.g., session_end_uri, session_last_event_type, session_last_created_at). | Join session-level last-event attributes onto user, order, or session aggregations without duplicating latest-event measures. | Compose with higher-level aggregations (count sessions by last event_type, count unique users by last traffic_source) after filtering rn = 1.
params.output_schema: id: event primary identifier from events_base.id (the event row id retained for the chosen latest event per session) | user_id: user identifier from events_base.user_id (which user generated the event) | session_id: session identifier from events_base.session_id (the session this event belongs to; partition key used by the row_number) | sequence_number: sequence index from events_base.sequence_number (tie-breaker ordering within a session) | created_at: event timestamp from events_base.created_at (used to determine most recent event; primary ordering) | ip_address: client IP from events_base.ip_address (geo/network attribute captured on the event) | city: city from events_base.city (geo attribute captured on the event) | state: state from events_base.state (geo attribute captured on the event) | postal_code: postal_code from events_base.postal_code (geo attribute captured on the event) | browser: browser string from events_base.browser (client user agent attribute stored on the event) | traffic_source: traffic_source from events_base.traffic_source (marketing/source attribution captured on the event) | uri: requested URI/path from events_base.uri (page/resource visited in the event) | event_type: event type from events_base.event_type (semantic event classification) | rn: row number computed by ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, sequence_number DESC) indicating ordering within the session; rn = 1 is the latest event for that session
params.grounded_columns: events_base.id | events_base.user_id | events_base.session_id | events_base.sequence_number | events_base.created_at | events_base.ip_address | events_base.city | events_base.state | events_base.postal_code | events_base.browser | events_base.traffic_source | events_base.uri | events_base.event_type
params.metric: rn = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY events_base.session_id ORDER BY events_base.created_at DESC, events_base.sequence_number DESC)  -- positional/ordering metric (non-aggregated). | No aggregated numeric metrics are produced by this view. All output columns are either raw event attributes or the row-number ordering value (rn).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on latest_event_per_session.user_id = users_base.id — safe because latest_event_per_session is at most one row per (session_id, rn) and when filtered to rn = 1 it is one-row-per-session; joining a one-row-per-session relation to a one-row-per-user dimension (users_base) will not duplicate session rows (each session maps to a single user row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_per_user_agg on latest_event_per_session.user_id = orders_per_user_agg.user_id — safe only if you are joining to an aggregation that is one-row-per-user. If orders_per_user_agg is one-row-per-user, joining will not duplicate sessions; confirm the target agg's grain before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on latest_event_per_session.user_id = orders_base.user_id only when you intend to allow multiple orders per user to multiply session rows; this is NOT safe if you want to preserve one row per session. To avoid duplication, either aggregate orders_base to one-row-per-user first (e.g., latest order or order counts) or restrict orders_base to a single order per user (e.g., by ranking and filtering). | do NOT join directly to order_items_base, products_base, order_items_enriched, inventory_items_base, or any other known one-to-many tables (order_items, products-per-order, inventory movements) without first aggregating them to the same grain (one-row-per-session or one-row-per-user) because those joins will multiply latest_event_per_session rows and thus duplicate any session-level measures or attributes. | do NOT join to sibling rank or window views (e.g., top_products_by_revenue_rank, orders_fulfillment_latency) without understanding their grain; many rank/window views are multi-row per entity and will produce duplicates unless you filter to a single row per join key. | safe composition pattern: filter this view to rn = 1 (latest_event_per_session WHERE rn = 1) to obtain one-row-per-session, then left join to one-row-per-user dimensions (users_base) or to one-row-per-session aggregations. When joining to multi-row datasets, first aggregate or select a single representative row (e.g., use ROW_NUMBER or GROUP BY) to avoid cardinality multiplication. | explanation why: the view itself is multi-row per session (it returns all events with an rn ordering). Only after filtering rn = 1 does it become one-row-per-session. Any join that assumes one-row-per-session must therefore be applied after that filter. Joins to one-to-many tables without prior aggregation will increase the number of rows per session, duplicating attributes drawn from this view.

views.description: Latest event per session determined by created_at and sequence_number tie-breaker. Exposes a row per session with the last event; useful for session-level endpoint URI, last event_type and timestamps. | Use for: session endpoint page/URI analysis; identify last touch traffic_source before purchase

views.name: top_products_by_revenue_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT psa.product_id AS product_id,
       psa.items_sold AS items_sold,
       psa.total_sales AS total_sales,
       psa.avg_sale_price AS avg_sale_price,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY psa.total_sales DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM product_sales_agg psa
grain: product_id -- one row per product with rank

params.description: Lists products with their sales metrics and a revenue-based rank (1 = highest total_sales).
params.when_to_use: Show top products by revenue or rank (leaderboards, reports). | Filter or paginate products by revenue_rank (e.g., top N products). | Compose product-level dashboards that need items_sold, total_sales, avg_sale_price, and a stable revenue rank. | Join product-level attributes (name, category) onto these sales metrics without changing the metrics.
params.output_schema: product_id: product identifier (sourced from product_sales_agg.product_id). One row per product_id — the view's grain. | items_sold: total quantity sold for the product (sourced from product_sales_agg.items_sold). This is a base aggregate metric computed in product_sales_agg. | total_sales: total revenue (monetary) for the product (sourced from product_sales_agg.total_sales). This is a base aggregate metric computed in product_sales_agg and is the ordering key for revenue_rank. | avg_sale_price: average sale price for the product (sourced from product_sales_agg.avg_sale_price). Derived/aggregated in product_sales_agg (likely total_sales / items_sold or similar). | revenue_rank: integer rank of the product when ordering by total_sales descending (computed here using RANK() OVER (ORDER BY psa.total_sales DESC)). Ties receive the same rank; ranks may skip values when ties occur.
params.metric: items_sold = <pre-aggregated metric from product_sales_agg; no further aggregation in this view> | total_sales = <pre-aggregated metric from product_sales_agg; used for ordering and ranking> | avg_sale_price = <pre-aggregated metric from product_sales_agg; typically derived as total_sales / items_sold in product_sales_agg> | revenue_rank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY product_sales_agg.total_sales DESC)  -- window function producing product-level rank based on total_sales
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base on product_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-product_id, so joining a one-row-per-product dimension (products_base) will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to distribution_centers_base or other product-level dimension on product_id — safe for the same reason as above. | DO NOT join this view directly to order_items_base, orders_base, events_base, order_items_enriched, or any other one-to-many detail table without re-aggregation, because those joins would duplicate rows and multiply items_sold/total_sales measures (product_sales_agg already contains aggregates over those detail rows). If you need to filter by attributes from a one-to-many table (for example, only include order_items with a certain property), first aggregate or filter at the detail level and then re-compute product-level aggregates (or join to a pre-aggregated view such as product_sales_agg produced with that filter). | When composing additional aggregations on top of this view (for example, sum total_sales across a category), treat items_sold and total_sales as additive measures that can be summed across rows (they are already aggregated at the product grain). Do not re-aggregate avg_sale_price by averaging the per-product avg_sale_price without weighting; to get a correct overall average price across multiple products, compute weighted_avg_price = SUM(total_sales) / SUM(items_sold) using the provided measures. | If you need per-product time slicing (e.g., monthly ranks), do not use this view (it has no time grain). Instead, use or create a time-partitioned product_sales_agg (if available) or recompute aggregates with a time dimension before ranking.

views.description: Products ranked by total_sales within product_sales_agg. Exposes total_sales and a revenue_rank so downstream queries can filter rank <= K to get top-K products. | Use for: top-k product lists by revenue (use revenue_rank <= K); banding products into revenue percentiles

views.name: orders_fulfillment_latency
views.body_sql:
SELECT oi.id AS id,
       oi.order_id AS order_id,
       oi.created_at AS created_at,
       oi.shipped_at AS shipped_at,
       oi.delivered_at AS delivered_at,
       CASE WHEN oi.shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.shipped_at - oi.created_at) ELSE NULL END AS time_to_ship,
       CASE WHEN oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.shipped_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.delivered_at - oi.shipped_at) ELSE NULL END AS time_ship_to_deliver,
       CASE WHEN oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.delivered_at - oi.created_at) ELSE NULL END AS time_to_deliver,
       AVG(CASE WHEN oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.delivered_at - oi.created_at) END) OVER (PARTITION BY oi.order_id) AS avg_time_to_deliver_per_order
FROM order_items_base oi
grain: id -- one row per order item

params.description: Per-order-item fulfillment timing metrics and per-order average delivery time (one row per order item).
params.when_to_use: Measure per-item fulfillment times (time to ship, time ship→deliver, time to deliver). | Compare fulfillment latency across items, orders, or other dimensions when joining on keys that do not multiply order items. | Compose order-level aggregates that need the item-level avg_time_to_deliver_per_order (already computed per order) without re-aggregation. | Build reports of delays, SLA compliance, or distribution of fulfillment times at the item or order level.
params.output_schema: id: identifier for the order item (derived from order_items_base.id) | order_id: identifier for the parent order of the item (derived from order_items_base.order_id) | created_at: item creation/timestamp (derived from order_items_base.created_at) | shipped_at: item shipped timestamp (derived from order_items_base.shipped_at) | delivered_at: item delivered timestamp (derived from order_items_base.delivered_at) | time_to_ship: interval/duration between shipped_at and created_at; expression = shipped_at - created_at (NULL if either timestamp missing) (derived from order_items_base.shipped_at and order_items_base.created_at) | time_ship_to_deliver: interval/duration between delivered_at and shipped_at; expression = delivered_at - shipped_at (NULL if either timestamp missing) (derived from order_items_base.delivered_at and order_items_base.shipped_at) | time_to_deliver: interval/duration between delivered_at and created_at; expression = delivered_at - created_at (NULL if either timestamp missing) (derived from order_items_base.delivered_at and order_items_base.created_at) | avg_time_to_deliver_per_order: windowed average of time_to_deliver computed per order (AVG(delivered_at - created_at) OVER (PARTITION BY order_id)); same value repeated for each item of the same order (derived from order_items_base.delivered_at and order_items_base.created_at)
params.metric: time_to_ship = CASE WHEN order_items_base.shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND order_items_base.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (order_items_base.shipped_at - order_items_base.created_at) ELSE NULL END | time_ship_to_deliver = CASE WHEN order_items_base.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND order_items_base.shipped_at IS NOT NULL THEN (order_items_base.delivered_at - order_items_base.shipped_at) ELSE NULL END | time_to_deliver = CASE WHEN order_items_base.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND order_items_base.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (order_items_base.delivered_at - order_items_base.created_at) ELSE NULL END | avg_time_to_deliver_per_order = AVG(CASE WHEN order_items_base.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND order_items_base.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (order_items_base.delivered_at - order_items_base.created_at) END) OVER (PARTITION BY order_items_base.order_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on orders_base.id = orders_fulfillment_latency.order_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-order_item; joining to the single order row will not duplicate the item-level rows or their derived durations. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_base on products_base.id = order_items_base.product_id (if product_id exists in order_items_base) only if product_id is one-to-one per order item; this view's rows are per item so joining to a single product row will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_base on users_base.id = orders_base.user_id only when joining via orders_base (orders_base is 1:1 to an order). Do not join directly to users_base using a 1:many relation that multiplies order rows. | do NOT join directly to order_items_enriched (a JOIN view) or any other one-to-many view/table that returns multiple rows per order_item without re-aggregation — because those joins can multiply this view's item rows and therefore duplicate time-based measures. | do NOT join to events_base or user_event_sessions_agg (event-level tables) on order_id or order_item id without first aggregating events to the same grain (one row per order_item or per order) — event tables are typically many events per item/order and will multiply rows and distort averages/sums. | when you need order-level aggregates (for example total_time_to_deliver_per_order), re-aggregate from this view grouped by order_id (e.g., SUM or AVG of time_to_deliver grouped by order_id) rather than joining a many-row dimension to avoid double counting. | if joining to any child/many relation is required, first aggregate the child to the order_item (id) or order (order_id) grain to preserve correctness; e.g., join a pre-aggregated events_per_order_item view ON id to ensure one-row-per-id alignment.

views.description: Calculate fulfillment latency metrics per order_item/order: shipment and delivery lag in seconds (or whatever epoch unit the timestamps use). Exposes derived latency columns for running/window analytics downstream. | Use for: fulfillment SLA and latency analysis; compare shipping performance by distribution center or product

views.name: user_lifecycle_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT u.id AS id,
       u.email AS email,
       u.age AS age,
       u.gender AS gender,
       u.country AS country,
       u.city AS city,
       u.traffic_source AS traffic_source,
       opa.orders_count AS orders_count,
       opa.items_ordered AS items_ordered,
       opa.first_order_at AS first_order_at,
       opa.last_order_at AS last_order_at
FROM users_base u
LEFT JOIN orders_per_user_agg opa
  ON u.id = opa.user_id

params.description: Per-user lifecycle summary combining user attributes with per-user order aggregates (orders count, items ordered, first/last order timestamps).
params.when_to_use: Report: user-level KPIs such as lifetime orders, items purchased, first/last order time and demographic/traffic_source breakdowns. | As a building block when composing cohort analyses or funnels where the grain is one row per user. | Joining to higher-level aggregations (e.g., country or traffic_source roll-ups) that aggregate these per-user metrics without re-aggregating raw orders. | Enriching user lists for downstream ML features (features per user: total orders, items ordered, recency).
params.output_schema: id: unique user identifier — from users_base.id | email: user email address — from users_base.email | age: user age — from users_base.age | gender: user gender — from users_base.gender | country: user country — from users_base.country | city: user city — from users_base.city | traffic_source: acquisition or traffic source for the user — from users_base.traffic_source | orders_count: total number of orders for the user — from orders_per_user_agg.orders_count (aggregate over orders_base.id grouped by orders_base.user_id) | items_ordered: total number of items ordered by the user — from orders_per_user_agg.items_ordered (aggregate over order_items_base.quantity or equivalent grouped by orders_base.user_id) | first_order_at: timestamp of the user's earliest order — from orders_per_user_agg.first_order_at (min(orders_base.created_at) per user) | last_order_at: timestamp of the user's latest order — from orders_per_user_agg.last_order_at (max(orders_base.created_at) per user)
params.grounded_columns: users_base.id | users_base.email | users_base.age | users_base.gender | users_base.country | users_base.city | users_base.traffic_source | orders_per_user_agg.user_id | orders_per_user_agg.orders_count | orders_per_user_agg.items_ordered | orders_per_user_agg.first_order_at | orders_per_user_agg.last_order_at
params.metric: orders_count = SUM(1) over orders grouped by orders_base.user_id OR explicit orders_per_user_agg.orders_count (pre-aggregated) | items_ordered = SUM(order_items_base.quantity) aggregated to orders_per_user_agg.items_ordered (pre-aggregated) | first_order_at = MIN(orders_base.created_at) aggregated to orders_per_user_agg.first_order_at | last_order_at = MAX(orders_base.created_at) aggregated to orders_per_user_agg.last_order_at
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables or views that are one-row-per-user (e.g., users_base) on users_base.id — safe because this view is one-row-per-user and the join preserves one row per user so the per-user measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to user-level aggregates (e.g., user_event_sessions_agg) on user_id — safe if the target is also one-row-per-user; confirm the sibling view's grain is one row per user before joining without re-aggregation. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., orders_base, order_items_base, order_items_enriched, events_base) without re-aggregating those tables up to user-level first, because joining a one-row-per-user view to a one-to-many relation will multiply that user's orders_count/items_ordered and distort measures. | If you need attributes from a one-to-many source (orders_base/order_items_base/events_base), either: (a) join to the corresponding pre-aggregated sibling view (orders_per_user_agg, product_sales_agg, user_event_sessions_agg) which are one-row-per-user or per-key, or (b) aggregate the one-to-many relation to user_id first (e.g., GROUP BY user_id) and then join — ensure the aggregation aligns to the same user_id key. | When composing higher-level rollups (country, city, traffic_source), aggregate orders_count and items_ordered via SUM(orders_count), SUM(items_ordered) over this view grouped by the desired dimension — this is safe because measures are already at user grain. | Avoid joining to sibling JOIN views that are one-to-many with respect to user (e.g., order_items_enriched) unless you explicitly re-aggregate after the join or restrict to a unique row per user (e.g., via ROW_NUMBER) — otherwise metrics will be multiplied.

views.description: One-row-per-user summary joining users_base to orders_per_user_agg to produce demographic plus order-activity features useful for customer segmentation. | Use for: build user segments for marketing; lifetime activity cohorts and retention
